meaning: Observe a possible numbered H token only; it can refer to indicated or added indicated hydrogen, or be syntactically ambiguous.
observable: numbered H token and character span
limitations: Does not determine fragment ownership, isotope meaning, atom mapping, or whether every tautomeric site is fixed.

capability: indicated hydrogen atom mapping and tautomer support
meaning: Indicated hydrogen can locate a ring hydrogen; added indicated hydrogen has different grammar.
observable: CML locants plus grammatical fragment ownership and candidate graph
result: UNKNOWN until unique ownership and all tautomer-sensitive sites are validated
limitations: Existing locant labels do not in general establish fragment ownership; a local H does not specify all other tautomeric sites.

meaning: Named functional groups constrain structure but a general suffix matcher cannot establish the complete tautomer without grammatical scope and mapped atoms.
observable: parsed name grammar, group locants, candidate atom and hydrogen mapping
limitations: Retained names, multiple tautomeric systems and implicit hydrogen placement require independent analysis.

meaning: Operational suffixes specify ionic centers in context, not solely by matching a substring.
observable: parsed suffix ownership, counterion counts and atom mapping
limitations: -ate may denote an ester and charged sites or counterions can be missing, repeated or distributed.

meaning: Nitro denotes a nitrogen-bound NO2 group; formal charge-separated drawings can represent a neutral group.
observable: mapped source nitro group and all charged atoms/components
result: UNKNOWN for source form until all charge and protonation sites are accounted for
limitations: Nitro presence alone does not justify every charge state or infer that a name lacks another ionic center.

meaning: An alias omitting a descriptor may be broader; two genuinely specific incompatible claims can conflict.
observable: independently verified per-claim dimension-specificity and source scope
result: Existing coarse broad-alias handling retained; no new admission rule
limitations: Parser-produced graphs do not establish alias scope, and the 18 primary alias-conflict records mostly include constitutional differences.
